drafted_from: the tool row in what-this-tool-does-and-how-to-run-it.json (its words, input schema and status) and the code it points to in this folder; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "When a new sales contract comes in, run the contract builder". Once this row is on, it sets a rule that runs a tool or workflow when something happens. It is off (status inactive) until the scheduling owner accepts the call shape; while it is off, the AI says so and does not pretend a schedule was kept.
no_lists_because: Rules are kept by the host, and this row does not store them.
instructions: 1. Ask your AI to set a rule in plain words: when something happens, run a tool or workflow.
2. The AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run and tool tool:run-when-something-happens with the rule's input.
3. The rule is kept by the host's rules list, not by this row; this row only answers.
4. Read the reply and confirm to the person what the rule now does.

worked_examples.title: Set a rule for new sales contracts
worked_examples.ask: When a new sales contract comes in, run the contract builder.
worked_examples.given: The person asks for a rule on new sales contracts.
worked_examples.hands_back: The reply says "unavailable" while this row is off, and no rule is kept. Once on, it returns the rule id "new-sales-contract" with enabled true.
